title: Indian Councils Act and Limited Representation in Bengal
subtitle: The 1861 Act authorized a nominated legislative council for Bengal, which began meeting in Calcutta in 1862.
summary: The Indian Councils Act 1861 restored legislative powers to the presidencies and authorized the Governor-General to establish provincial legislative councils. In Bengal, the council was constituted in January 1862 under Lieutenant-Governor John Peter Grant, with nominated members; it did not create an elected legislature or responsible government. The measure widened consultation within colonial administration while retaining executive control.
heroTagline: A limited, appointed opening for provincial legislation in Bengal.
whyItMatters: The Bengal council created a formal provincial forum where selected non-official members could participate in lawmaking, but membership remained appointed and authority limited. It is an early stage in the history of legislative institutions in Bengal, not the introduction of popular representation.
